rules.description: `get` goes before `set` or `init`, and `add` before `remove`. The fix swaps the two accessors (not offered when a comment stands between or in them).

An async method returning Task or ValueTask has a name that does not end in `Async`. Overrides, explicit interface implementations and `Main` are left alone (their names are not the method's to choose). Renaming needs the binding layer, so there is no fix.

A comparison with the constant on the left: `null == x` is `x == null`, `1 < x` is `x > 1`. Without the type layer a constant is a literal, `nameof`, `int.MaxValue`-style member or an expression of those; a named constant on the left is not recognised.

The summary of a constructor starts with "Initializes a new instance of the <see cref="T"/> class" (struct), "Initializes static members of the ..." for a static constructor, and a private constructor may say "Prevents a default instance of the ... from being created". The `<see>` is compared with the name of the type. The fix puts the standard sentence before the text.
`Debug.Assert` without a message, or with a constant blank one. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Assert` is. No fix.
`Debug.Fail` with a constant blank message. With the type layer the call is checked against `System.Diagnostics.Debug`; without it any call written `Debug.Fail` is. No fix.
The summary of a finalizer starts with "Finalizes an instance of the <see cref="T"/> class.". The `<see>` is compared with the name of the type. The fix puts the standard sentence before the text.
No space between `#` and the directive keyword (`#if`, not `# if`).
A documentation line (`///`) starts with a single space. More spaces are allowed to indent continuation lines, not on the first line of the comment; a tab or no space is always reported.
A `<param>` without a `name` attribute, or with an empty one. No fix.
A `<param>` without text. Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

A partial type or method without a documentation comment (or with an empty one). Each part is checked on its own; StyleCop (SA1601) accepts one documented part, which needs the other parts of the project. Which elements need documentation follows StyleCop's defaults: everything but private members.
A documentation comment of a partial type or method without `<summary>` or `<content>` (and without `<inheritdoc />`). Each part is checked on its own. No fix.
The `<summary>` (or `<content>`) of a partial type or method has no text. Each part is checked on its own. No fix.
A documented partial generic type (with a `<summary>`) that has no `<typeparam>` for one of its type parameters. Each part is checked on its own. No fix.
A `<returns>` without text. Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.
A documented method or delegate that does not return `void` and has no `<returns>` (and no `<inheritdoc />`). Private members are left alone, as in StyleCop's defaults. No fix.

A documentation comment without `<summary>` (and without `<inheritdoc />`) on a type, member or field that StyleCop's defaults ask to document: everything but private members. Partial types and methods are `doc-partial-summary-required`. No fix.
A `<summary>` without text (`<summary></summary>`; `<summary />` is left alone, as StyleCop does). Partial types and methods are `doc-partial-summary-text`. No fix.

The last text of an element of a documentation comment does not end with a period (`.` or `.)`). Each paragraph of `<para>` and `<note>` is checked, a paragraph that ends in a colon (except the last), `-or-` and `<seealso>` are left alone, and an inline element (`<see />`, `<c>`, ...) at the end counts as not ending with a period. The fix adds the period, or replaces a trailing comma or semicolon with it.
A `<remarks>`, `<example>`, `<exception>` or `<permission>` element without text, written `<remarks></remarks>` or `<remarks />`. No fix.
A `<typeparam>` without a `name` attribute, or with an empty one, in the documentation of a generic class, struct, interface, method or delegate. No fix.
A `<typeparam>` without text (`<typeparam name="T" />` counts), in the documentation of a generic class, struct, interface, method or delegate. No fix.
A property's `<value>` without text (`<value></value>`; `<value />` is left alone, as StyleCop does). Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.
The file name, up to its first dot and ignoring case, is the name of the first type in the file; a generic type may also be written `Name{T,U}`. Not checked when that type is partial. No fix.

example.input: class Orders { }

rules.description: `<inheritdoc />` without `cref` on a type without a base list, or on a member that neither overrides nor implements anything (a constructor whose signature matches a base constructor is fine). No fix.

Members are out of order. Compared with the member before, in the order of the `element_order` option: the kind (fields, constructors, finalizers, delegates, events, enums, interfaces, properties, indexers, operators, methods, structs, classes; in a namespace or file: namespaces, delegates, enums, interfaces, structs, classes), the access (public, internal, protected internal, protected, private protected, private), constants before other fields, static before instance members, readonly fields before the others. A trait only counts between members that agree on the traits listed before it. No fix: moving members would have to take their comments and directives along.

options.description: The traits that decide the order, most important first. A trait that is left out is not checked.
options.name: element_order

rules.description: A comment between the head of an `if`, `else`, `while`, `do`, `for`, `foreach`, `lock`, `try`, `catch`, `finally`, `switch`, `checked` or `unchecked` and its `{`. Put it inside the block or above the statement.
A `<summary>` that starts with the text Visual Studio generates, "Summary description for ...". Skipped when the comment has `<inheritdoc />`. No fix.

`new S()` of a value type with an implicit parameterless constructor and no initializer: write `default(S)` (`Guid.Empty`, `CancellationToken.None`, `IntPtr.Zero`, the enum member with value 0 where they exist). No fix for a target-typed `new()`.
A `<placeholder>` element in a documentation comment. No fix.

A `///` comment that holds only text, no XML element: a plain comment written with documentation slashes. The fix writes `//`, unless the comment documents a declaration (it would remove documentation).
Two elements of one documentation comment with the same text (a copied and pasted `<param>`, for example). Empty elements and "The parameter is not used." are ignored. No fix.
An attribute with empty parentheses: `[Foo()]` is `[Foo]`. Parentheses with a comment in them are left alone.
A catch block with no statements and no comment swallows the exception silently.

An anonymous method with an empty parameter list: `delegate() { }` is `delegate { }`. Parentheses with a comment in them are left alone. The fix is unsafe: without a parameter list the method also converts to delegate types that have parameters, which can change which overload is chosen.

A lone `;` is a statement that does nothing. A statement labelled `label: ;` is allowed. The fix removes the statement (its whole line when it is alone on it), or turns an empty loop or `if` body into `{ }`; it is not offered for the only statement of a switch section. Overlaps compiler CS0642 for `if (x);`.
A `#region` inside a block (a method, accessor or lambda body, or any block in one); regions belong between members. No fix.

`#region` hides code behind a label. Reported on every `#region` outside a block (a region inside a block is `no-region-in-body`'s), in disabled `#if` branches too; no fix, because removing a pair is a judgment call.
A `<returns>` on a method or delegate that returns `void`. The fix removes the element with its line when it is alone on it.
`base.M()` or `base[i]` where the type does not override the member, so `this` binds to the same one. The fix writes `this`.

`int?` instead of `Nullable<int>` or `System.Nullable<int>`. Name-based: a type of your own called `Nullable` is reported too. Not reported in `using` aliases, `nameof`, `typeof(Nullable<>)` and before a member access (`Nullable<int>.Equals`).

A member or element access on an expression the compiler's nullable analysis says may be null. Only code under `#nullable enable` is checked. Off by default: the compiler reports the same thing as CS8602.

A property summary starts with "Gets", "Sets" or "Gets or sets" ("Gets a value indicating whether" and so on for `bool`), as the property's accessors reachable from outside the type say. The type is read from the declaration (`bool`, `Boolean`, `System.Boolean`). The fix replaces the start of the text and lower-cases what follows.

A property summary says "Gets or sets" while one of the accessors is not reachable from outside the type (`private set`, `internal get` on a public property). The fix replaces the start of the text with the one that matches the visible accessor.
A `using` directive inside a namespace whose name is not written fully qualified (it resolves relative to the enclosing namespace). The fix writes the full name, unless it has type arguments.

A `using` directive that nothing in the file needs (the compiler's hidden CS8019, IDE0005 in the SDK analyzers). Not reported in a file that has compiler errors or `#if` regions, because unresolved or inactive code could be the one using it.
One attribute per attribute list: `[A, B]` becomes `[A]` and `[B]`. Lists on parameters and type parameters are left alone. The fix is not offered when the list has a comment in it.

One field or event per declaration: `int a, b;` becomes `int a;` and `int b;`, each with the attributes, modifiers and type of the original. The fix is not offered when the declaration has a comment in it.
A file holds one class or record: every later one is reported, more parts of the first class (when it is partial) excepted. Structs, interfaces, enums and delegates are not counted. No fix.
A file declares one namespace: every later one, nested ones included, is reported. No fix.
`SuppressMessage` needs a `Justification` that says something: not missing, `null`, empty, blank or `"<Pending>"`. Matches the attribute by name. No fix.

A tuple type in the signature of a method, constructor, property, indexer, conversion operator or delegate whose elements have no names. Overrides and implementations of interface members are left alone (their names are not the member's to choose). No fix.

A statement that can never run. At `fast` depth this is the statement after a `return`, `throw`, `break`, `continue` or `goto`; with the flow layer it also covers constant conditions and calls that do not return (`does_not_return` in `semantics:`). Only the first statement of a run is reported. Removing it is offered as an editor quick fix only, because unreachable code usually signals a bug. Off by default: the compiler already reports unreachable code (CS0162) and the SDK analyzers add IDE0035.

example.input:
class A { int F() { return 1; G(); G(); }
 int H(int x) { if (false) { G(); } throw null; x++; } int G() => 1; }

options.description: Treat the code after a call that never returns (`[DoesNotReturn]`,                       `does_not_return` in `semantics:`) as unreachable. The compiler does not,                       so turn this off to report exactly what it reports (CS0162).
options.name: non_returning_calls

rules.description: A value is stored in a local variable and no path reads it before it is overwritten or the variable goes out of scope (a dead store). Variables that are captured or whose address is taken are not checked; a variable that is never read at all is reported by `unused-variable` instead. Overlaps the SDK analyzer IDE0059 (unnecessary assignment).

example.input: class A { int F() { int n = 0; n = G(); return n; } int H() { int m = 0; m = 1; m = G(); return m; } int G() => 1; }

rules.description: A private field, method, property or event that no file of the project uses (`analysis: deep`). Members with attributes, overrides, interface implementations, `extern` and `partial` methods are left alone. Overlaps the SDK analyzers IDE0051 (unused private member) and IDE0052 (unread private member).

A local variable or catch variable that is never used (the compiler's CS0168), or is only assigned constants and never read (CS0219). Variables captured by lambdas or local functions count as used. Off by default: the compiler already warns (CS0168, CS0219).

A lambda instead of an anonymous method. The fix is offered when the anonymous method has a parameter list and no comment before its body; `delegate { }` without one converts to delegate types with any parameters, so it has no fix.

A numeric literal cast to `long`, `ulong`, `uint`, `float`, `double` or `decimal` when the literal's own type differs: `(long)1` is `1L`. Not reported for hexadecimal and binary literals cast to a floating-point type, which have no suffix.
`string.Empty` instead of `""` (or `@""`). Not reported where a constant is required: `const`, attribute arguments, default parameter values, `case` labels and patterns.

`ValueTuple<int, int>` and `ValueTuple.Create(a, b)` where tuple syntax `(int, int)` and `(a, b)` is available (not inside an expression tree). The fix is offered for types and `ValueTuple.Create` calls.

`using` directives of a file or namespace are out of order: System first (`system_first`), names in alphabetical order (`compare`), and with the options `static_position` and `alias_position` set to `after`, `using static` directives after the plain ones and aliases after those, each group sorted. `global using` and `using unsafe` stay where they are, and a list restarts at a directive that has a preprocessor directive in front of it (the fix leaves such lists alone). Comments on lines of their own stay where they are; a comment after a directive moves with it. Overlaps the SDK analyzers' `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` .editorconfig key.

options.description: `ordinal` compares code points; `culture` ignores case (and puts                           punctuation before digits before letters, a lower-case name before                           an upper-case one that is otherwise equal); `culture_ignore_case`                           leaves names that differ only in case in their order.
options.name: compare

options.description: `after`: `using static` directives come after the plain usings, sorted (System ones first with `system_first`); `keep`: they stay where they are.
options.name: static_position

options.description: `after`: alias directives come after all other usings, sorted by alias name; `keep`: they stay where they are.
options.name: alias_position
